title: Liquid Chromatography Coupled to Refractive Index or Mass Spectrometric Detection for Metabolite Profiling in Lysate-based Cell-free Systems
protocol: Thaw previously prepared E. coli lysates on ice.
Prepare S30 buffer by filtering it through a 0.20 µm pore filter.
Mix glucose, glutamate salts, ATP, Coenzyme A, NAD+, Bis-Tris buffer, and dipotassium phosphate in the S30 buffer to create an energy mix.
Combine components to prepare final reactions with 4.5 mg/mL of total lysate protein in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Add E. coli lysates as the final component of the reaction mixes.
Incubate reactions at 37 °C for their respective timeframes.
Terminate reactions by adding an equal volume of 5% trichloroacetic acid to each sample's final reaction volume.
Dilute each sample with sterile water at twice the reaction volume.
Mix the same volume of 5% trichloroacetic acid as the total final reaction volume with lysate prior to adding the rest of the reaction components.
Vortex the samples thoroughly.
Centrifuge the samples on a benchtop microcentrifuge at 11,600 x g for 5 minutes.
Transfer supernatants containing organic analytes to clean tubes.
Store the samples at -20°C if HPLC analyses are to be conducted on a different day.
Thaw stored samples on ice before proceeding to the next step.
Filter each supernatant with a 0.22 µm pore filter using centrifuge tube filters and centrifuging at 16,300 x g for 1 minute.
Transfer each filtrate to a clean HPLC glass vial.
Load HPLC glass vials onto the HPLC autosampler tray.
Prepare samples for standard curve generation.
Prepare a stock solution of target analytes dissolved in S30 buffer at equimolar amounts above the starting concentration of glucose in the CFME reactions.
Perform 1:1 (v/v) serial dilutions from the stock solution to obtain triplicate 50 µL solutions with final concentrations ranging from 0 µM to the stock concentration.
Dilute each solution with 50 µL of 5% trichloroacetic acid and 100 µL of sterile water.
Repeat steps for standard curve generation with each batch of samples to ensure accurate quantification of metabolite concentrations.
Under a fume hood, prepare a sterilized 5 mM sulfuric acid solution from deionized and filter-sterilized water.
Add approximately 550 µL of a 98% HPLC grade sulfuric acid solution to 2 L of water to prepare 5 mM sulfuric acid.
Incubate the 2 L bottle of 5 mM sulfuric acid in a water bath set to 35 °C.
Attach tubing with a solvent filter from the solvent bottle to the degasser module and connect it to the pump module.
Equip the HPLC instrument with the HPLC column in line with the RID module.
Place the HPLC column in the 35 °C water bath if no column thermostat is available.
Prepare the RID module for analysis at 35 °C using Chromatography Data System (CDS) software.
Right-click on the Pump Module > Method and set the flow rate to 0.55 mL·min-1, selecting On to start the pump.
Right-click on the panel corresponding to the RID Module > Method and set the temperature of the RI detector module to 35 °C, selecting On to start warming up the RI detector module.
Select On for the Purge Reference Cell for at least 15 min when using a fresh solvent or for 1 h if different solvents flowed through the RI detector prior to this setup.
Keep the pump and RI detector on to achieve a stable baseline.
Select Method > New Method from the menu bar.
Select Method > Save Method as [MethodName].
Select Method > Edit Entire Method > Instrument/Acquisition.
Set the flow to 0.55 mL·min⁻¹ within the Binary Pump tab.
Set the solvent input on the pump module to 100% for isocratic elution.
Set Pressure Limits to 0 and 400 bar, with a Stoptime of 30 min.
Set the Injection Volume to 50 µL within the Sampler tab.
Set Draw Speed, Eject Speed, and Draw Position to 200 µL·min⁻¹, 200 µL·min⁻¹, and -0.5 mm.
Set Optical Unit Temperature to 35 °C within the RID tab.
Select Acquire for Signal and >0.2 min for Peakwidth under Signal in the RID tab.
Select the Positive option for Signal Polarity and the On option for Automatic Zero Before Analysis under Advanced in the RID tab.
Set Analog Output to 5% Zero Offset and 500,000 nRIU for Attenuation under Advanced in the RID tab.
Save the method by selecting Method > Save Method.
Load the method by selecting Method > Load Method > [MethodName].
Create a sequence table for autosampling.
Start the HPLC-RID system for data acquisition.
Select Sequence > New Sequence Template from the menu bar.
Select Sequence > Save Sequence Template as [SequenceTemplateName].S.
Select Sequence > Sequence Table.
Append 'n' rows corresponding to 'n' vials in the sequence table.
Input vial positions and sample names under Vial and Sample Name, respectively.
Select the Method generated in step 3 from the Method Name dropdown menu for each row.
Input 50 µL as Inj/Vial (Injection per Vial) for each row.
Click Apply to save changes.
Save the sequence template by selecting Sequence Template > Save Sequence Template.
Load the sequence template by selecting Sequence > Load Sequence Template > [SequenceTemplateName].S.
Right-click the panel RID Module > Control > Off Recycling Valve to direct solvent flow through the RID detector to waste after achieving a stable baseline on the online plot.
Select Sequence from the menu bar, then select Sequence > Run to start data acquisition.
Select Data Analysis view from the View menu.
Locate the Sequence Filename from the File List on the left-hand side of the screen.
Go to the Signal View Selection > RID Signal to view the sample chromatograms.
Select a row corresponding to a high concentration standard sample from the top panel on the screen.
Take note of the retention times for the target analyte peaks on the displayed chromatogram.
Extract peak areas for each target analyte from chromatograms of the standards and the reaction samples.
Discern whether the peaks-of-interest are well integrated by the software.
Draw the red line as the base of each peak to obtain an accurately integrated area under the curve.
If automatic integration fails, select the Manual Integration button from the Integration Tool Set.
Manually draw a peak base to integrate the peak area if necessary.
Select the Cursor tool from the Common Tool Set to click on properly integrated peaks.
Highlight peak area and retention time as a table row on the bottom panel of the screen.
Export peak areas by selecting File > Export > Integration Results.
Quantify target analyte concentrations using standard curves.
Plot peak area values vs. known concentrations of samples in a spreadsheet.
Right-click on the plotted data, Add Trendline > Format Trendline > Display Equation on Chart.
Use equations from standard curve trendlines to convert peak area values to concentrations for every analyte from each sample.
Calculate average peak areas and standard error values across triplicates for data visualization.
Set up triplicate reactions per time point (except time zero) on ice as described in 1.1-1.2.
Use a final concentration of 100 mM 13C6-glucose in the reactions instead of glucose.
Incubate the reactions at 37 °C for 1 h, 2 h, and 3 h.
Flash freeze reactions in liquid nitrogen to terminate them after incubation.
Store terminated reactions at -80 °C unless conducting same-day analysis.
Prepare 50 mL of extraction solvent for LC-MS/MS analysis.
Combine and vortex 20 mL of acetonitrile, 20 mL of methanol, and 10 mL of water in a 50 mL centrifuge tube along with 0.199 mL of formic acid to make a 0.1 M solution.
Chill the solvent to 4 °C during extraction and store the solvent at -20 °C when not in use.
Pipette an equivalent volume of the extraction solvent (i.e., 50 µL) to each sample on the day of analysis.
Add the extraction solvent before samples completely thaw out if they were frozen, to prevent reactivation of glucose metabolism.
Perform all sample processing steps on ice.

Recapitulate time zero by pipetting the final volume of extraction solvent (i.e., 50 µL) to an appropriate volume of lysate for the desired final concentration in the reaction (i.e., of 4.5 mg/mL in a 50 µL reaction volume).
Add the rest of the reaction components as specified.
This acidification step precipitates lysate enzymes before they significantly metabolize glucose.
Incubate the samples in extraction solvent on ice for 30 min with gentle shaking.
Centrifuge the samples at 21,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer 50 µL of the supernatant to autosampler vials.
Load the vials onto the tray within the 4 °C autosampler.
Store the rest of the supernatant at -20 °C for future analyses.
Dissolve 77.08 mg of ammonium acetate in 950 mL of water and 50 mL of isopropanol to prepare Solvent A.
Mix 650 mL of acetonitrile, 300 mL of water, and 50 mL of isopropanol along with 77.08 mg of ammonium acetate to prepare Solvent B.
Connect the solvent bottles containing Solvents A and B to the pump module.
Purge the system at a high flow rate to remove air contamination.
Equip the system with a C18 reversed-phased column (30 cm length, 75 µm inner diameter, 5 µm particle diameter).
Condition the column by flowing 100% solvent B and gradually increasing Solvent A to 100%.
Open Tune Plus software to edit a tune file for the MS method.
From the File menu bar, open a preinstalled negative mode tune file.
Select ScanMode on the menu bar, then select Define Scan Window.
Set the microscan time setting for MSn to 1 for both Ion Trap and FT.
Go to settings for Nano-ESI Source and set Spray Voltage to 4 kV.
Modulate Spray Voltage until an acceptable electrospray is generated.
Save the tune file.
Generate a new LC method using the Setup Wizard of the instrument's data acquisition software.
Open Roadmap > Sequence Setup > Wizard.
Skip the Temp Control step in the setup wizard.
Select Multistep under Flow Gradient Pump Options.
Insert 7 lines and set the flow rate for each row to 0.1 mL·min-1.
From 0-3 min, deliver 100% solvent A.
From 3-9 min, introduce a gradient from 100% solvent A to 20% solvent B.
From 9-19 min, introduce a new gradient from 20% solvent B to 100% solvent B.
From 19-27 min, hold at 100% solvent B.
From 27-28 min, set the gradient back to 100% solvent A.
From 28-44 min, rinse and recondition of the column for subsequent runs by holding at 100% solvent A.
Lower the flow rate to 0.03 mL·min-1 upon completion of the run to conserve the solvent when the LC is not in use.
Apply Default settings for Sampler Options > Pump Pressure as the Acquisition Option.
Use Default Acquisition Time options.
Use Default Pump Pressure options.
Create an MS/MS method by selecting the Orbitrap Velos Pro MS icon from the sidebar on the Instrument Setup window.
Click on New Method > Data Dependent MS/MS.
Set Acquire Time to the length of the LC run (i.e., 44 min).
Set Segment to 1.
Set Scan Events to 11.
For Tune File, select the edited file from step 8.1.
NOTE: The first event is an MS1 precursor scan using the Fourier Transform MS (FTMS).
Set Analyzer to FTMS and Polarity to Negative for Event 1.
Use a Resolution of 30,000 and Normalized Collision Energy of 35 V for MSn Settings in Event 1.
Set Scan Ranges from 50 m/z for first mass to 1800 m/z for last mass in Event 1.
Set Analyzer to Ion Trap for Events 2 through 11.
Select Dependent Scan and Enable Dynamic Exclusion with a 30 s repeat duration and 120 s exclusion duration for Events 2 through 11.
Set Mass Determined from Scan Event to 1 for all MS2 events (2 through 11).

Set each MS2 scan event to detect an nth Most Intense Ion, starting with 1 as the nth Most Intense Ion in Event 2 and increasing by 1 for each subsequent event until Event 10 detects the 10th most intense ion.
Save the method setup as [Method_Name].meth.
Set up a Run Sequence using the LC-MS/MS system's data acquisition software.
Insert rows in the table for each sample.
Set Inj Vol to 5 µL for each row.
Set Position to the vial's respective position on the autosampler tray.
Input file names as sample names.
Set the desired file path for run results.
Run blank vials containing Solvent A at the start and between sets of triplicate samples.
Highlight all File Names in the Sequence.
Select Actions > Run Sequence > OK from the menu bar.
Open MZmine and import the '.raw' output files.
From the menu bar, select Raw Data Methods > Raw Data Import.
Construct a list of peaks distinguishing between MS1 and MS2 scans.
From the menu bar, select Raw Data Methods > Feature Detection > MS/MS Peaklist Builder.
Set m/z Window to 0.01.
Set Time Window to the length of the run.
Select Negative as Polarity under set filters.
Select Centroided as the Spectrum Type.
Go to Feature List Methods > Feature Detection > Peak Extender.
Set m/z Tolerance to 0.005 m/z or 10 ppm.
Set Minimum Height to 1E3.
Remove duplicate peaks.
Go back to Feature List Methods > Filtering > Duplicate Peak Filter.
Set m/z Tolerance to 0.005 m/z or 10 ppm.
Set RT Tolerance to 5 min.
Process triplicate samples together and leave out blanks.
Go back to Feature List Methods > Normalization > Retention Time Calibration.
Set m/z Tolerance to 0.005 m/z or 10 ppm.
Set RT Tolerance to 3 min absolute (min).
Set Minimum Standard Intensity to 1E3.
Align peaks from all files by m/z and retention time.
Go back to Feature List Methods > Alignment > RANSAC Aligner.
Set m/z Tolerance to 0.005 m/z or 10 ppm.
Set RT Tolerance and RT Tolerance After Correction to 44 and 39 min, respectively.
Set RANSAC Iterations to 0.
Set Minimum Number of Points to 10%.
Set Threshold Value to 1.
Tick the option Require Same Charge State.
Correct for any data points that may have been lost in prior steps in Feature List Methods > Gap Filling > Peak Finder.
Set Intensity Tolerance to 50%.
Set m/z Tolerance to 0.005 m/z or 10 ppm.
Set RT Tolerance to 3 min.
Enable RT correction.
Calculate the masses of 13C-labeled metabolites from glucose metabolism for targeted search.
Calculate the monoisotopic mass of each target compound using its molecular formula and elemental isotopic masses.
Subtract the mass of one proton (1.007276 Da) from the monoisotope mass to obtain the negative mode mass [M-H]-.
Use calculated masses of 13C-labeled metabolites to search and annotate m/z features from MZmine results.
Calculate the mass error (ppm) for each possible hit using the provided equation.
Consider experimental m/z values with less than 15 ppm mass error as putative annotations in analysis.
Manually check spectra of putative annotations on a quality browser to confirm annotations.
Draw a line under the desired range of retention times on the total ion chromatogram.
Right-click on the spectrum and input a range of masses that encompass the target analyte's m/z.
Check whether the putative annotations have distinct peak signals above the noise.
Calculate the average peak areas and the standard errors of positive annotations across biological replicates for each time point.
Visualize the data on a bar graph to observe trends in glucose metabolism.
